author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Israel said Thursday that its military had destroyed an underground Hezbollah complex at the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, marking a new development in the conflict along the border.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz said the operation completed the consolidation of what Israel describes as a security zone. They said Israeli forces would remain in the area to prevent Hezbollah from rebuilding positions. The ridge is roughly 15 kilometers, or 10 miles, from the Israeli border.

The Israeli military said the underground network extended more than two kilometers and contained rockets, missiles, drones, anti-tank weapons, mines and explosives. It also described the site as a command complex for Hezbollah’s Badr unit. Those battlefield claims were made by Israel and were not independently verified in the source report.

Lebanon’s state news agency reported a powerful blast that was felt around Nabatieh. The destruction and Israel’s statement that its troops will stay in the area underscore the continuing risk of escalation and leave questions about the duration and legal status of the military presence.
dek: Israeli leaders said forces demolished a tunnel network at the Ali al-Taher ridge, about 15 kilometers from the border.
headline: Israel says it destroyed Hezbollah underground complex in Lebanon
